By examining the equation for different values of \( n \) and using the periodicity of the derivative, we derive that: 1. For any \( x \) and positive integers \( n \) and \( m \), we can express \( f(x + n + m) \) in two ways:
   \[
   f(x + n + m) = f(x + n) + m f'(x + n)
   \]
   \[
   f(x + n + m) = f(x) + (n + m) f'(x)
   \]
   Equating these two expressions, we get:
   \[
   f(x) + (n + m) f'(x) = f(x) + n f'(x) + m f'(x + n)
   \]
   Simplifying, we find:
   \[
   m f'(x) = m f'(x + n)
   \]
   Dividing by \( m \), we obtain:
   \[
   f'(x) = f'(x + n)
   \]
